title: Commercial Fusion Energy in 2026: Applied Judgement Diagnostic

questions.stem: A congressional staffer asks whether ITER's newly installed sixth sector module means the machine will soon send electricity to the grid. What is the accurate response?
questions.question: A congressional staffer asks whether ITER's newly installed sixth sector module means the machine will soon send electricity to the grid. What is the accurate response?
choices: ITER is primarily exploratory science and is not designed or intended to produce electricity.
ITER will produce net electricity once all nine sector modules are installed.
ITER is designed to demonstrate commercial net energy gain by the mid-2030s.
ITER is a fission facility, so it will generate electricity from uranium.
questions.answer: ITER is primarily exploratory science and is not designed or intended to produce electricity.
rationales: CRS states ITER is primarily an exploratory science initiative and is not designed or intended to produce electricity [S1].
Installing all nine modules completes the core, but CRS says ITER is not intended to produce electricity [S1][S4].
The mid-2030s deployment target belongs to the U.S. DOE roadmap, not to ITER's purpose [S2].
ITER is a fusion tokamak, not a fission facility using uranium [S1][S2].
questions.explanation: ITER tests burning-plasma science and materials; it is not a grid power plant.

questions.stem: An investor asks whether the U.S. roadmap to deploy early-stage fusion plants by the mid-2030s is fully funded. What does Reuters report?
questions.question: An investor asks whether the U.S. roadmap to deploy early-stage fusion plants by the mid-2030s is fully funded. What does Reuters report?
choices: Success hinges on more federal funding, according to industry leaders.
The roadmap is fully funded because the Office of Fusion was created in November 2025.
Private developers have already achieved net energy gain, so public funding is unnecessary.
The strategy depends mainly on ITER, which is designed to produce electricity.
questions.answer: Success hinges on more federal funding, according to industry leaders.
rationales: Reuters reports the strategy's success hinges on more federal funding, industry leaders say [S2].
The Office of Fusion was created in November 2025 to coordinate implementation, not to guarantee funding [S2].
Reuters states private developers have not yet achieved net energy gain [S2].
ITER is exploratory and not designed to produce electricity, so it cannot be the main electricity-producing plank [S1].
questions.explanation: The mid-2030s goal is a strategy, not a funded guarantee.

questions.stem: A startup plans a deuterium-tritium plant and assumes tritium can be purchased at scale. Which engineering gap does Reuters identify as central to securing fuel?
questions.question: A startup plans a deuterium-tritium plant and assumes tritium can be purchased at scale. Which engineering gap does Reuters identify as central to securing fuel?
choices: Breeding blankets needed to secure a steady supply of tritium.
Neutron-resistant structural materials, because tritium supply is already solved.
Plasma-facing components, which eliminate the need for any fuel processing.
Lithium blankets needed to breed deuterium rather than tritium.
questions.answer: Breeding blankets needed to secure a steady supply of tritium.
rationales: Reuters names breeding blankets to secure a steady supply of tritium, a nuclear fuel [S2].
Neutron-resistant materials are also a challenge, but Reuters pairs them with breeding blankets for tritium and does not say tritium supply is solved [S2].
Plasma-facing components are a milestone area, but they do not remove the need for fuel processing or breeding [S2].
Breeding blankets breed tritium, not deuterium; deuterium is distinct [S2].
questions.explanation: Tritium scarcity makes breeding blankets a fuel-supply requirement, not an optional extra.

questions.stem: A reporter reads that ITER installed the sixth of nine sector modules in July 2026. How many modules remain, and when is the final module targeted?
questions.question: A reporter reads that ITER installed the sixth of nine sector modules in July 2026. How many modules remain, and when is the final module targeted?
choices: Three modules remain; the final module is targeted for 2027.
Six modules remain; the final module is targeted for 2030.
Two modules remain because two-thirds of the core is in place.
One module remains because the last Korean sector is installed.
questions.answer: Three modules remain; the final module is targeted for 2027.
rationales: ITER says the sixth of nine modules is in place and the final module is on track for 2027 [S4].
Six of nine are installed, so three remain; 2030 is not the target given [S4].
Two-thirds of nine is six installed, leaving three, not two [S4].
The last Korean-manufactured vacuum vessel sector is installed, but other sectors remain [S3][S4].
questions.explanation: Six of nine installed leaves three, with completion targeted in 2027.

questions.stem: Two analysts brief a committee: one cites 28 U.S. fusion companies from a 2026 FIA dataset; another says around 30. How should the briefing explain the gap?
questions.question: Two analysts brief a committee: one cites 28 U.S. fusion companies from a 2026 FIA dataset; another says around 30. How should the briefing explain the gap?
choices: It likely reflects the same tally at slightly different moments: 28 is the exact FIA 2026 figure and around 30 is a rounding.
It proves the U.S. fleet grew from 28 to 30 companies within the same year.
The 28 figure is wrong because the ANS article says around 30.
The sources give no U.S. fusion company counts at all.
questions.answer: It likely reflects the same tally at slightly different moments: 28 is the exact FIA 2026 figure and around 30 is a rounding.
rationales: S2's exact 28 is tied to a named Fusion Industry Association 2026 dataset, while S3's around 30 is an explicit rounding, so they likely reflect the same tally at slightly different moments [S2][S3].
The sources do not report a measured month-by-month growth from 28 to 30; calling it proof overreads a rounding [S2][S3].
S3's around 30 is a rounding, not a correction that invalidates the exact 28 [S2][S3].
Both sources do give counts: 28 [S2] and around 30 [S3].
questions.explanation: Treat exact and rounded company counts as one tally, not evidence of growth.

questions.stem: A procurement analyst reads that four of nine ITER vacuum vessel sectors were made in Korea and Europe made the other five. Which sector is the newly installed sixth module built around?
questions.question: A procurement analyst reads that four of nine ITER vacuum vessel sectors were made in Korea and Europe made the other five. Which sector is the newly installed sixth module built around?
choices: Vacuum vessel sector #1, the fourth and final Korean-manufactured sector.
A European sector, because Europe is the ITER host.
Sector #6, because it was the sixth module installed.
The first Korean-manufactured sector, because Korea completed its program.
questions.answer: Vacuum vessel sector #1, the fourth and final Korean-manufactured sector.
rationales: ITER states the sixth module is built around vacuum vessel sector #1, the fourth and final sector manufactured in Korea [S4].
Europe made five sectors, but the sixth module uses the final Korean sector, not a European one [S4].
Module installation order does not equal sector number; the sixth module is built around sector #1 [S4].
Sector #1 is the fourth and final Korean sector, not the first [S4].
questions.explanation: Module sequence and sector numbering are different; the sixth module carries Korean sector #1.

questions.stem: A state economic development official wants to attract a fusion company claiming grid connection in the early 2030s. What should the official verify first, given the sources?
questions.question: A state economic development official wants to attract a fusion company claiming grid connection in the early 2030s. What should the official verify first, given the sources?
choices: That the claim aligns with DOE's mid-2030s roadmap and that private developers have not yet achieved net energy gain.
That ITER has achieved ignition and will supply electricity to the grid.
That NIF's gain factor above one has already solved commercial breakeven.
That the company has a breeding blanket because tritium is abundant.
questions.answer: That the claim aligns with DOE's mid-2030s roadmap and that private developers have not yet achieved net energy gain.
rationales: Reuters reports a DOE strategy targeting early-stage plant deployment by the mid-2030s and says private developers have not yet achieved net energy gain [S2].
CRS says ITER is exploratory and not designed or intended to produce electricity [S1].
Wikipedia says NIF's gain factor above one still requires efficiencies orders of magnitude higher for engineering or economic breakeven [S6].
Reuters says breeding blankets are needed to secure tritium, a scarce fuel, not because tritium is abundant [S2].
questions.explanation: Match developer claims against the roadmap timeline and the still-unmet net-energy-gain milestone.

questions.stem: A journalist asks whether NIF's fusion energy gain factor above one proves a commercial power plant is ready. What is the accurate answer?
questions.question: A journalist asks whether NIF's fusion energy gain factor above one proves a commercial power plant is ready. What is the accurate answer?
choices: No; efficiencies orders of magnitude higher are required for engineering breakeven or economic breakeven.
Yes; a gain factor above one is the same as economic breakeven.
Yes; NIF is the only lab with gain above one and therefore sells electricity.
No; no laboratory has ever demonstrated a gain factor above one.
questions.answer: No; efficiencies orders of magnitude higher are required for engineering breakeven or economic breakeven.
rationales: Wikipedia states NIF demonstrated gain above one, but efficiencies orders of magnitude higher are required for engineering breakeven or economic breakeven [S6].
Wikipedia distinguishes gain above one from engineering and economic breakeven, so it is not the same [S6].
NIF demonstrated gain above one, but that does not mean it sells electricity [S6].
Wikipedia says NIF is the only laboratory to have demonstrated a gain factor above one as of 2025 [S6].
questions.explanation: Scientific gain above one is not engineering or commercial breakeven.

questions.stem: A policymaker proposes cutting domestic fusion R&D because ITER assembly is ahead of schedule. What is the strongest source-based objection?
questions.question: A policymaker proposes cutting domestic fusion R&D because ITER assembly is ahead of schedule. What is the strongest source-based objection?
choices: ITER is exploratory science not designed to produce electricity; U.S. roadmap gaps in materials and tritium breeding remain.
ITER will produce electricity, so domestic R&D is redundant.
ITER's schedule proves commercial net energy gain has already been achieved.
ITER is a fission project, so its progress cannot help fusion.
questions.answer: ITER is exploratory science not designed to produce electricity; U.S. roadmap gaps in materials and tritium breeding remain.
rationales: CRS says ITER is exploratory and not designed or intended to produce electricity, while Reuters identifies remaining U.S. roadmap gaps in neutron-resistant materials and tritium breeding blankets [S1][S2].
CRS explicitly says ITER is not designed or intended to produce electricity, so it cannot replace domestic R&D on that basis [S1].
Reuters says private developers have not yet achieved net energy gain, regardless of ITER assembly progress [S2].
ITER is a fusion tokamak, not a fission project [S1][S2].
questions.explanation: ITER assembly progress does not close the U.S. materials, fuel-cycle, and net-gain gaps.

questions.stem: A logistics analyst reads the sixth ITER module lift took 30 hours and the suspended load with rig weighed nearly 1,400 tonnes. What was the module's approximate weight?
questions.question: A logistics analyst reads the sixth ITER module lift took 30 hours and the suspended load with rig weighed nearly 1,400 tonnes. What was the module's approximate weight?
choices: About 1,100 tonnes.
Nearly 1,400 tonnes, because that is the module weight.
120 tonnes, because sector 3 carries 120 sensors.
30 tonnes, because the lift took 30 hours.
rationales: ITER states the sector module weighed approximately 1,100 tonnes, while the suspended load with lifting rig was nearly 1,400 tonnes [S4].
Nearly 1,400 tonnes is the load including the lifting rig, not the module alone [S4].
120 is the number of sensors on sector 3, a different component and metric [S3].
30 is the number of hours the lift took, not a weight [S4].
questions.explanation: Separate payload weight from rig-inclusive load when reading lift specs.

questions.stem: A technology scout asks whether global fusion development is limited to ITER and a few U.S. startups. What does the IAEA outlook add?
questions.question: A technology scout asks whether global fusion development is limited to ITER and a few U.S. startups. What does the IAEA outlook add?
choices: It describes dozens of fusion plant concepts at various stages of development worldwide.
It reports exactly nine tokamak sector modules worldwide.
It counts 28 global plant concepts, matching the U.S. company total.
It says no fusion plant concepts exist outside ITER.
questions.answer: It describes dozens of fusion plant concepts at various stages of development worldwide.
rationales: The IAEA World Fusion Outlook 2025 outlines dozens of fusion plant concepts currently at various stages of development worldwide [S5].
Nine is ITER's sector-module count, not a global plant-concept count [S4][S5].
The 28 figure is U.S. fusion companies [S2], not IAEA's global plant-concept count [S5].
The IAEA describes dozens of plant concepts worldwide, not only ITER [S5].
questions.explanation: The global pipeline is broader than ITER and the U.S. startup fleet.

questions.stem: An assembly scheduler reads that three ITER vacuum vessel sectors now rest on gravity supports. What does ITER say this confirms?
questions.question: An assembly scheduler reads that three ITER vacuum vessel sectors now rest on gravity supports. What does ITER say this confirms?
choices: The configuration is stable enough to begin preparations for vacuum vessel welding.
Vacuum vessel welding is complete and the tokamak is ready for plasma.
All nine sector modules are installed.
The machine has achieved burning plasma ignition.
questions.answer: The configuration is stable enough to begin preparations for vacuum vessel welding.
rationales: ANS reports ITER said three sectors on gravity supports confirmed the configuration is sufficiently stable to begin preparations for vacuum vessel welding [S3].
The source says preparations for welding can begin, not that welding is complete [S3].
Only three sectors were on supports at that stage, not all nine [S3].
Ignition is ITER's key operating goal, not a status confirmed by sector supports [S1][S3].
questions.explanation: Support stability is a prerequisite for welding prep, not completion or ignition.
